one_month_reasoning: AMAT's own FQ4 FY26 report is on 2026-11-12, outside the window ending 2026-10-29. Inside the window is a dense run of customer and peer prints. Micron reports FQ4 on 2026-09-30 after the close; it has guided FY27 capex to rise every quarter from the ~$10B FQ4 run-rate, so the risk is mainly in the tone, not the direction. Samsung prelims come ~Oct 7, ASML Q3 on Oct 14, TSMC Q3 with first 2027 capex colour ~Oct 15, Lam on Oct 21, Intel ~Oct 22, SK hynix late October and hyperscaler capex ~Oct 27-29; KLA may land at the window's edge. The BIS Affiliates Rule decision has reportedly moved to ~Jan 9-10 2027, outside the window. Each print can move semi-cap 5-10% in a day, but their sign isn't knowable in advance, and the backdrop is mixed. The capex path is still rising (SEMI raised its 2028 WFE forecast in September). Against that, the stock rebounded +23% from its $415.38 Sept 16 closing low, including +5.2% on 9/29, and short-term reversal and momentum roughly cancel. I stay symmetric around ~$511 with monthly sigma ~16.5% (60% / 3.5, lognormal); this is unchanged from round 1 apart from rounding.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods. (1) NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $22.5 (FY28 consensus $23.85 less a ~6% late-cycle haircut) x 22x plus $8/share net cash = $503. (2) Unhaircut FY28 consensus $23.85 x 21x (roughly AMAT's ~20-22x long-run average P/E, applied to forward EPS as a cycle-aware multiple) plus $8 net cash = $509. (3) FY28 FCF of ~$16.7/share at a 3.4% yield plus $8 net cash = $499. Weighted 45/35/20 this gives ~$505, roughly spot.

bear.story: The cycle turns earlier than SEMI expects. AI or HBM capex digestion, memory spending cuts, or the BIS Affiliates Rule returning after the ~Jan 10 2027 deadline cut FY28 estimates 20-25% to ~$18. The multiple falls to ~16-17x. This matches the 2018 (-30%+) and 2022 (~-50%) semi-cap drawdowns.

base.story: WFE grows ~20% in 2027 as SEMI forecasts. FY27 EPS lands ~$18.5 and the FY28 path holds around $22-24. The forward multiple compresses from ~26x to ~22-23x as the market prices a late cycle. EPS growth roughly offsets de-rating, so the stock ends near fair value, slightly above spot.

bull.story: The upcycle extends into 2028-29: SEMI's upgrade to $220B 2028 WFE proves conservative, advanced packaging and GAA/HBM intensity lift share and gross margin, FY28 EPS moves to $27+ and the multiple holds ~28-30x. The stock retakes the $723 closing high and exceeds it.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$335 (~15x my $22.5 NTM EPS, and ~19% below the $415 September closing low), the market would be pricing a real WFE downturn and deep estimate cuts, not ordinary 60%-vol noise. For that to happen, SEMI's still-growing 2027-28 WFE path would have had to fail, through memory or AI capex cuts, the Affiliates Rule returning in January 2027 or a recession.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established that my decisive growth input was stale. I used SEMI's Dec-2025 forecast (+7-8% equipment growth in 2027), but the July 14 2026 mid-year release has WFE +23.1% in 2026, +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028 to ~$200B. I verified this, and found SEMI raised 2028 WFE further to ~$220B at SEMICON Taiwan (Digitimes, 2026-09-01). My +8% FY28 growth assumption therefore goes. I now anchor on FY28 consensus EPS of $23.85, with a smaller ~6% late-cycle haircut to $22.5. I also dropped the Polymarket recession figure as a valuation driver, since it came from a blocked snippet and is macro context only. I replaced the mixed-basis 19x trailing median with a 21-22x forward multiple, which sits between the trailing average and the ~25x forward 5-year average quoted by data vendors. I also dropped the FY27 x 25x leg, because at Sep-2027 the market values FY28. Net cash is now $8/share. Fair value rises from $455 to ~$505, close to spot. Base rates still drive the shape. AMAT has 60% realized vol, fell 29% from its $723 closing high to a $415 low within three months, and semi-cap has drawn down ~30% in 2018 and ~50% in 2022; all of this justifies a fat left tail. The distribution is lognormal with median ~$520 (fair value ~$505 plus a modest nod to still-rising WFE and upward revisions) and sigma ~0.50, with the left tail thickened slightly for the Jan-2027 Affiliates Rule deadline and cycle-turn risk. That gives P(>=512) = 0.515, vs 0.49 in round 1. Scenarios are $310/$530/$810 at 25/50/25. Research was limited to ~9 queries, and GuruFocus and MarketScreener fetches failed or returned the wrong page, so the FY28 consensus relies on the supervisor's MarketScreener read. No option data was used.
